relevance_note: Cohort of nine Alexander disease patients with per-patient GFAP variants and symptoms: 'Here we report on the course of the disease in nine AxD patients.'
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand. Table 1 has patients as columns (column header 'Patient' with values 1-9; the text uses 'Patient N', so labels follow rule 1). A Python script in my scratch directory transcribed Table 1 and Table 2 cells into spans of the form '<row label> | <cells up to that patient>'; I checked its output against the tables and every span is verified verbatim by script. Table 1 legend defines '-' as absent ('- = feature is absent'), so '-' cells are excluded with the legend as a second span; empty cells, 'NA' and 'unclear' are not reported; ages are onset ages per the caption; 'temp.' = temporary; 'a.s.' = after stroke; 'd.' = dementia (patient 7, developmental delay row, recorded as dementia, not as developmental delay); '10a' (patient 4, basal ganglia row) recorded as written with no ISO conversion. Multi-age MRI cells such as '2y, 4y' are time points of one finding, not stacked per-patient values; no ' / '-stacked cells occur. The worst-GMFCS row, the steroid row of Table 1, Table 4 (ADSS scores) and Table 2 care items other than blind/deaf and G-tube were not turned into features. Composite checklist items were excluded only when every part was addressed: 'macrocephaly -' does not exclude 'macrocephaly or megalencephaly', 'ataxia -' does not exclude 'ataxia or cerebellar signs', 'ocular movement abnormalities -' does not exclude '... or diplopia', 'spastic paraparesis -' does not exclude limb weakness. Recurrent vomiting is observed only for patient 5 ('episodes of vomiting'); table 'vomiting' cells for others do not state recurrence. Cognitive decline: delays (patients 1-4) not counted as decline. Patient 5: Table 1 marks autonomic dysfunction '-', but the text reports sleep apnoea, which the checklist item includes, so the checklist item is observed. Dysarthria for patients 1, 2 and 4 comes from the group statement 'dysarthria was seen in almost all seven patients (except for patient 3...)'. Novel variants c.1118A>G (patient 4) and c.1013T>C (patient 5) 'arose de novo' (ACMG PS2 printed) but no parental testing is described, so inheritance is 'not reported' under the de novo rule. The c.170C>T (p.Ala57Val) variant of patient 4 and his father is not explicitly attributed to a gene (context implies GFAP), so gene_symbol_as_stated is 'not reported'. Patient 3's 'microdeletion 15p13.2q13.3' recorded as printed (reference 35 concerns 15q13.3). Out of scope: patient 7's children ('unaffected', not tested). Patient 8 has no genetic test (autopsy diagnosis) and no variant row. Contradictions/inconsistencies: patient 2 Table 1 'cognitive abnormalities' '-' vs text 'later also cognitive, delay' (both rows emitted; checklist cognitive decline not reported); patient 5 'cognitive abnormalities' '-' vs text dyscalculia and concentration problems; patient 6 last report 'at the age of 32 years' in text vs 'last follow up was at the age of 33 years' and Table 1 '33y' (Table 1 used); patient 6 Table 1 ataxia blank vs text gait ataxia at one year; patient 4 Table 1 hypotonia '10y' vs text hypotonia before ten months; patient 1 first seizure 'one and a half years' vs table '1y' and patient 4 'three and a half years' vs '3y' (caption says ages are rounded); Introduction says 'seven individuals' for care data vs nine patients overall.
